_comment: Example machine-specific guard rules. Copy to ~/.omnisci/guard-rules.json to use.
The built-in rules cover what is dangerous anywhere: rm, find -delete, shred,
truncate, mkfs, rsync --delete, qdel, git push, git reset --hard. Anything that
is only a rule on YOUR machine belongs here instead, because a refusal message
that assumes someone else's setup is worse than no rule at all.
The two below are worked examples of that shape, for a machine with no TeX
installed where papers are compiled elsewhere. They are illustrations of how to
write a local rule, not recommendations: delete them and write your own.
verdict is deny or ask. `command` matches in command position only, so a rule for
`rm` does not fire on `npm rm`. `contains` matches anywhere in the command line.
A refusal should always name the alternative: refusing without one makes a model
stall or go looking for a way around, which is worse than the original request.
You can also switch off a built-in by id: {"disableRules": ["qdel"]}.

rules.reason: 这台机器上不跑 LaTeX 编译：没有装 TeX，而且编译日志很长，反复调错烧掉的 token 不成比例。注意这不是让你换个方式编译，是取消「本地验证编译」这个目标本身。改完 .tex 交给外部编译服务，回复里如实写明「未本地验证」。
这台机器上不安装 TeX 发行版（apt / docker / conda / brew 一律不行，全量镜像有好几个 GB）。不要再探测本机 TeX 环境，也不要寻找替代编译途径。
